messages:
Mia (Product Designer): dropped a focused prototype for the model catalog compare flow: https://www.figma.com/file/abc. Key decision points: filter precedence, compare-table density vs readability, pin/undo pattern, and badge accessibility. throw quick reactions pls. :coffee:
Raj (Frontend): skimmed it. The dense table looks great on wide screens but cramped at 1280px. Recommend collapsing non-critical cols and offering a 'show details' toggle per row.
Leah (Research): users in the last round wanted a lightweight summary row for scans, with the ability to expand only the rows they care about. Also they repeatedly used region + latency filters together.
Ava (Design PM): noted. Can we add a small "Recent / Starred" filter chip to the left? That was very effective for power users.
Mia (Product Designer): yep adding Recent + Starred. For pin UI I'm trying 2 patterns: 1) inline pin toggle with confirm toast, 2) modal selector. Leaning to inline to avoid context-switch. Thoughts?
Raj (Frontend): inline toggle + small confirm/undo toast is best for speed. Modal interrupts flow. We'll implement optimistic update with rollback on error.
Connor (Infra): backend note: optimistic pinning needs a conditional PUT with version etag to avoid overwriting concurrent changes. We can add an If-Match header on /routes/:id/pin. If conflict, return 409 with current pinned version.
Leah (Research): microcopy suggestion for the undo toast: "Pinned v2 to /checkout — Undo". Keep it short and include route name. Test participants liked explicit route context.
Mia (Product Designer): good microcopy. Also want to make pin targets >= 40px and use both icon + label so screen-reader users and motor-impaired people have an easier hit.
Raj (Frontend): will size the hit area and add sr-only text. Also adding role="button" and aria-pressed to reflect state.
Connor (Infra): on badges: we compute three signals (latency P50, cost per 1k tokens, and quality score). Rendering all badges for 200 models on page load is expensive. Suggest client-side lazy fetch for badge details and server-side bundled minimal summary for initial render.
Mia (Product Designer): propose placeholder chips with aria-busy and aria-label "metrics loading". When loaded, chips include icons and numerical text, e.g., "⚡ 18ms" with sr-only "Latency: 18 milliseconds".
Leah (Research): in a11y tests color alone confused users. Use icon+text and ensure contrast ratio >= 4.5. For badges that show severity (good/ok/poor) include an accessible label like "Performance: Good".
Ava (Design PM): ok action items: (A) add Recent/Starred filters, (B) collapse noncritical columns, (C) inline pin + undo toast, (D) badge lazy-load + a11y remap. Prioritize A/C/D for next sprint.
Raj (Frontend): I'll pick up C and D. For D I'll implement skeletons and a small client cache to avoid refetch on tab changes.
Connor (Infra): I'll add ETag support and conflict payload for pin endpoint. Also can add a bulk badge pre-warm API for users who request >50 items.
Leah (Research): I'll draft the tooltip copy for each badge and run a 5-person quick remote test once the skeletons are in place. Example tooltip: "Latency (P50): 18ms. Cost: $0.12 per 1k tokens. Quality: 92% on internal eval."
Mia (Product Designer): thanks. One more UX nit: keyboard navigation inside the compare table needs to preserve focus when rows collapse/expand. We should avoid traps where focus jumps to top.
Raj (Frontend): agree. Plan: keep focused DOM node stable, use focus management when toggling rows, and expose arrow-key navigation between cells.
Design-bot: figma-snapshot: https://cdn.redwood.ai/design/snap-1742100345-compare-2.png
Ava (Design PM): schedule a 20-min sync Friday to review the small tests and final microcopy. If no blockers, aim to ship pin and badge changes in the next release. :rocket:
